intervals.label: construction
intervals.quote: Most detector systems will be installed and ready for data taking by mid 2008 when the LHC is scheduled to start operation

end.note: Ends at the LHC-wide start of Long Shutdown 3 (June 2026); ALICE cannot record collisions the LHC is not delivering.

intervals.label: operating
intervals.note: The original ITS1/MWPC-TPC configuration operated 2009-2018; the upgraded ITS2/GEM-TPC configuration (ALICE 2) operates from 2021. Both are recorded as a single 'operating' interval since the detector identity (detector:alice) persists across the upgrade; the upgrade itself is a separate interval below.

intervals.label: ALICE 2 upgrade (new ITS2 pixel tracker, GEM-based continuous-readout TPC)
intervals.quote: In 2021, the collaboration completed a major upgrade, denoted ALICE 2, to enhance its detector capabilities and continue its scientific journey at the LHC in Runs 3 and 4.

end.note: CERN schedule: the LHC resumes operation in mid-2030; the rest of the CERN complex restarts in stages from mid-2028.

intervals.label: Long Shutdown 3 / ITS3 and FoCal upgrade
intervals.locator: home.cern/science/long-shutdown-3, item of 5 August 2026 "The LHC is being warmed up from near absolute zero to room temperature"
intervals.note: The ITS3 (new inner tracking layers) and FoCal (forward calorimeter) upgrades are approved for installation during Long Shutdown 3. The bounds and the sources' wording are those of experiment:alice, whose interval note also records that the 2024 and 2026 ALICE-related sources use older LS3 dates than CERN's mid-2030 schedule.
intervals.quote: Two detector upgrades of ALICE ... have recently been approved for installation during the next long shutdown of the LHC

name: ALICE detector
notes: specs.total_mass/length/diameter reflect the as-built (2008) detector; the ALICE 2 upgrade (2021) replaced the ITS and TPC internals but no source consulted gives updated overall mass/dimension figures, so the original detector-paper values are kept with a note.
Placed at site:cern-point-2-alice, whose coordinate is an approximate geocoder-derived campus point (see that record's notes) rather than a surveyed cavern coordinate.
The detector record carries the same Long Shutdown 3 interval and status as experiment:alice, so that the two agree.

summary.plain: A 10,000-tonne detector at CERN built to study collisions of lead nuclei. Layers of tracking and identification detectors sit inside a large recycled magnet, surrounded by a forward arm that catches muons, letting physicists reconstruct the thousands of particles each collision produces.
summary.technical: General-purpose heavy-ion detector: six-layer silicon Inner Tracking System, cylindrical Time-Projection Chamber, TOF/HMPID/TRD particle-identification arrays and PHOS/EMCal calorimeters inside the 0.5 T L3 solenoid (reused from LEP), plus a forward muon spectrometer (2-9 degrees) with a dipole magnet and 14 tracking/trigger chamber planes. Upgraded (ALICE 2: new ITS2 pixel tracker, GEM-based continuous-readout TPC) for LHC Run 3.

technology.quote: ALICE consists of a central barrel part, which measures hadrons, electrons, and photons, and a forward muon spectrometer.
technology.value: Central barrel of silicon/gas tracking, PID and calorimetry detectors inside a solenoid magnet, plus a forward muon spectrometer
